extracted.intended_audience: news executives, editors, newsroom journalists, and media organisations interested in editorial standards and verification
extracted.subtask_description: Summarises BBC editorial and verification standards for producing trustworthy journalism, including sourcing, verification, impartiality (due weight), and public-facing fact‑checking practices used by the BBC Verify unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict editorial guidelines & staff training
rubrics_metrics.description: Every employee is led by strict editorial guidelines and trained at length on the standards they’re to follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BBC emphasises that scale and reach are only possible when all staff adhere to the same editorial standards; training is long-form and organisation-wide to ensure consistency across its presence in 118 countries and 40+ languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-hand sourcing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is placed on reporters who are 'on the ground' in the places they report from rather than 'parachuting' in; first-hand sourcing underpins credibility and breadth of reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact and statistics checking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify numerical claims and statistical assertions rather than repeating them; this is listed as a core example of the BBC’s editorial practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify important caveats and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and communicate important caveats and limitations in reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should flag uncertainties and limits of evidence so audiences understand the boundaries of what is known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate authenticity of documentary and digital material
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate the authenticity of documentary evidence and digital material before publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes forensic inspection of media (e.g., spotting jump cuts), searching for corroborating postings on other platforms, and checking metadata/usage to detect manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroborate claims and allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Corroborate claims and allegations made by contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not publish uncorroborated allegations; seek independent confirmation and multiple sources where possible to substantiate assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh, interpret and contextualise claims (including statistical claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Weigh, interpret and contextualise claims, including statistical claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should place claims in context, explain relevance and limitations, and interpret what evidence means rather than presenting raw claims without analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due weight (impartiality informed by evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply 'due weight' rather than simple symmetry between opposing viewpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impartiality at the BBC means assessing whether different viewpoints carry the same evidentiary weight; for example, report climate science as the established evidence-base and do not give denialist views equal prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local presence / 'boots-on-the-ground' reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer reporters who are located within the communities/regions they cover rather than temporary or external reporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being embedded locally allows reporters to provide breadth and scale and reduces reliance on surface-level or second-hand accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of verification to audiences (public fact‑checking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make verification processes transparent to audiences by showing how checks were done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Through the BBC Verify brand the newsroom 'lifts the curtain' on tools, techniques and technology, explaining not just what the BBC knows but how it knows it — increasing trust through openness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated forensic verification capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain specialised teams (forensic journalists and expert talent) focused on verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BBC Verify comprises dozens of forensic journalists and cross-BBC experts whose remit includes fact checking, verifying video, countering disinformation, analysing data, and explaining complex stories — demonstrating organisational commitment and resource allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forensic multimedia verification techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Use forensic techniques to analyse multimedia (e.g., detect editing/jump cuts, check distribution across platforms, verify naming/details).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the team analysed a deceptive video by spotting jump cuts, searching for the video on credible sources, and noting misuse of an individual's name to demonstrate fabrication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate social media algorithms and misinformation flows
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively study how social media algorithms distribute content to understand how misinformation spreads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects like the 'Undercover Voters Investigation' create representative social media profiles and monitor algorithmic recommendations over time to document what kinds of false claims or violent rhetoric are being suggested to users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and assess audience impact and safety risks for journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise and document the risks journalists face (e.g., online abuse) and consider these impacts in editorial strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BBC notes that journalists working on disinformation beats are often subject to high levels of online abuse, which has operational and safety implications for how verification work is conducted and publicised.
